ap_statistics-m08.stem: A researcher wants to select a simple random sample of $12$ from $80$ employees by using a table of random digits. Which of the following procedures should the researcher use?

options.text: Number the employees from 01 to 80, read the table 1 digits at a time, and choose the first $12$ numbers that are read, even if a number is read twice.
options.why: Reading 1 digits at a time cannot produce every label, and accepting repeats does not give $12$ different individuals.

options.text: Number the employees from 01 to 80, read the table 2 digits at a time, and subtract 80 from any number that is larger than 80.
options.why: Subtracting makes some labels more likely than others, so not every individual has the same chance.

options.text: Number the employees from 01 to 80, read the table of random digits 2 digits at a time, skip any number that is not from 01 to 80 and any repeat, and continue until $12$ different employees are chosen.
options.why: Every individual has a label of the same length, every label is equally likely to be read, and ignoring invalid labels and repeats gives a simple random sample without replacement.

options.text: Number the employees from 01 to 80 and choose every $6$th individual from a random starting point.
options.why: This is a systematic sample; not every group of individuals has the same chance of being chosen, so it is not a simple random sample.
